records.name: Civil Resolution Tribunal
records.description: Canada's first online tribunal, resolving strata, small claims up to $5,000, vehicle accident, intimate image, and society and cooperative disputes.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. Created under the Civil Resolution Tribunal Act; launched July 13, 2016 (CRT about page).

records.name: British Columbia Review Board
records.description: Tribunal constituted under the Criminal Code that makes and reviews dispositions for accused persons found unfit to stand trial or not criminally responsible on account of mental disorder.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

records.name: Building Code Appeal Board
records.description: Resolves disputes under the Building Act about whether a matter conforms to a provincial building regulation such as the BC Building and Plumbing Codes.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. A member of the Building and Safety Standards Branch serves as board secretary (board page).

records.name: Community Care and Assisted Living Appeal Board
records.description: Hears appeals of licensing, registration and certification decisions about community care facilities, assisted living residences and early childhood educators under the Community Care and Assisted Living Act.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

records.name: Employment Standards Tribunal
records.description: Hears appeals of determinations issued by the Director of Employment Standards under the Employment Standards Act and the Temporary Foreign Worker Protection Act.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. Established November 1, 1995 (EST about page). The Ministry of Labour 2026/27 service plan also calls it one of 'the Ministry's three tribunals' (legislative responsibility), so ministry-of-labour-2017 is an alternative parent.

records.name: Energy Resource Appeal Tribunal
records.description: Hears appeals of certain orders, penalties and permitting decisions of the BC Energy Regulator under the Oil and Gas Activities Act as amended in 2023.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. Former name Oil and Gas Appeal Tribunal: the old ogat.gov.bc.ca domain linked from the tribunal-sector page redirects to bcerat.ca, and ERAT decisions carry OGAT file numbers.

records.name: Environmental Appeal Board
records.description: Decides appeals of certain government decisions under nine provincial statutes on environmental issues such as water licences, contaminated sites, pesticides and hunting licences.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. EAB site: 'established under the Environment Management Act (1981)'; now operates under the Environmental Management Act.

records.name: Financial Services Tribunal
records.description: Hears appeals of enforcement decisions by the Insurance Council of BC, the Superintendents of Real Estate, Pensions and Financial Institutions, and the Registrar of Mortgage Brokers.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. Established in 2004 under s. 242.1 of the Financial Institutions Act (FST about page).

records.name: Forest Appeals Commission
records.description: Decides appeals of certain decisions under five provincial statutes on forests and environmental issues, now operating under the Forest and Range Practices Act.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

records.name: Health Professions Review Board
records.description: Reviews certain registration and complaint decisions of the health profession regulatory colleges, now under the Health Professions and Occupations Act.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. HPRB site now says it is established under the Health Professions and Occupations Act (in force April 1, 2026).

records.name: Hospital Appeal Board
records.description: Hears medical practitioners' appeals of hospital board of management decisions affecting hospital privileges under the Hospital Act.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. 'Originally established as the Medical Appeal Board in 1973' (HAB about page).

records.name: Mental Health Review Board
records.description: Conducts review panel hearings on whether people certified or detained involuntarily in provincial mental health facilities should remain so under the Mental Health Act.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. 'Established in April 2005' (MHRB home page).

records.name: Passenger Transportation Board
records.description: Independent tribunal that licenses and regulates taxis, ride-hail, limousines, shuttles and inter-city buses in British Columbia.
records.note: Listed in the Ministry of Attorney General 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; not in the Transportation and Transit appendix and not on the tribunal-sector page. Inference: the tribunal-sector page names 19 AG tribunals, so PTB would make up TASD's stated 20.

records.name: Property Assessment Appeal Board
records.description: Second level of appeal for BC property assessments under the Assessment Act, after the Property Assessment Review Panels.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

records.name: Safety Standards Appeal Board
records.description: Adjudicative tribunal created under section 43 of the Safety Standards Act that hears appeals under that Act, the Homeowner Protection Act and the Building Act.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division. The Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs 2026/27 service plan also lists it among that minister's organizations, so ministry-of-housing-and-municipal-affairs-2024 is an alternative parent.

records.name: Skilled Trades BC Appeal Board
records.description: Hears appeals under section 45 of the Skilled Trades BC Act about SkilledTradesBC decisions on trainees, authorizations and credentials.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

records.name: Surface Rights Board
records.description: Resolves disputes between landowners and companies that need access to private land to explore for or produce Crown-owned subsurface resources such as oil, gas, coal, minerals and geothermal.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Attorney General (tribunal-sector page); listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; one of the 20 tribunals supported by AG's Tribunal and Agency Support Division.

records.name: British Columbia Ferry Commission
records.description: Independent regulator under the Coastal Ferry Act that sets the price cap on fares for BC's coastal ferry operators and approves major capital expenditures.
records.note: Regulator, not a TASD tribunal. Listed in the AG 2026/27 service plan Appendix A; its website is titled 'Office of the BC Ferries Commissioner'.

records.name: Workers' Compensation Appeal Tribunal
records.description: Final level of appeal in BC's workers' compensation system, independent of WorkSafeBC, established under the Workers Compensation Act.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Labour (tribunal-sector page); also named in the Labour 2026/27 service plan.

records.name: Employment and Assistance Appeal Tribunal
records.description: Hears appeals of SDPR decisions on income and disability assistance, and of MCFD decisions under the Child Care Subsidy Act.
records.note: Administratively accountable to SDPR (tribunal-sector page); the Tribunal Chair reports to the Minister of SDPR (eaat.ca about page).

records.name: British Columbia Farm Industry Review Board
records.description: Supervises BC's regulated agricultural marketing boards and commissions and hears marketing, farm practices and BC SPCA animal custody appeals and complaints.
records.note: Created in 2003 by combining the BC Marketing Board (1934) and the Farm Practices Board (1997) (BCFIRB 'Learn about' page). Supervises the 8 marketing boards and commissions in the AF service plan, which are not recorded here.

records.name: Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch
records.description: Regulates licensing and permits for liquor and private cannabis retail establishments, manufacturers and events, and inspects licensees.
records.note: Agriculture and Food took responsibility in July 2025 (AF service plan). The PSSG service plan says oversight is shared with AF from July 17, 2025 and that compliance and enforcement stay with PSSG.

records.name: Independent Gambling Control Office
records.description: BC's gambling and horse-racing regulator under the Gaming Control Act, overseeing BCLC, charitable gaming and horse racing and administering Gambling Support BC.
records.note: Replaced the Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch (GPEB) on April 13, 2026. The Gaming Control Act was introduced by PSSG (news release 2025PSSG0067). The BCLC 2026/27 service plan still names GPEB in PSSG.

records.name: Disciplinary and Professional Conduct Board
records.description: Nine B.C. Teachers' Council members, appointed by the Minister, who hear teacher conduct and competence matters and certification appeals referred by the Commissioner for Teacher Regulation.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Education (tribunal-sector page).

records.name: Commissioner for Teacher Regulation
records.description: Independent statutory decision maker under the Teachers Act who oversees the discipline process for certified teachers in BC.
records.note: Regulatory office, not a tribunal. It is not in the Education 2026/27 service plan appendix, so the parent comes from its gov.bc.ca page location.

records.name: B.C. Teachers' Council
records.description: Sets standards under the Teachers Act for teachers' education, competence and professional conduct, and approves post-secondary teacher education programs.
records.note: Regulatory standards body listed in the Education 2026/27 service plan Appendix A.

records.name: Health Care Practitioners Special Committee for Audit Hearings
records.description: Hears practitioners and decides whether the Medical Services Commission should recover payments after audits of health care practitioners.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Health (tribunal-sector page); acts under audit powers the Medical Services Commission delegated.

records.name: Medical Services Commission
records.description: Manages the Medical Services Plan under the Medicare Protection Act, ensuring reasonable access to medical care and managing payment for medical services.
records.note: Listed in the Health 2026/27 service plan Appendix A. The gov.bc.ca page URL tried returned 404.

records.name: Patient Care Quality Review Boards
records.description: Six independent review boards under the Patient Care Quality Review Board Act that review care complaints left unresolved by a health authority's Patient Care Quality Office.
records.note: Six boards shown as one dot.

records.name: Emergency Medical Assistants Licensing Board
records.description: Examines, registers and licenses BC emergency medical assistants, including first responders, under the Emergency Health Services Act.
records.note: Listed in the Health 2026/27 service plan Appendix A. The gov.bc.ca page URL tried returned 404.

records.name: Health Professions and Occupations Regulatory Oversight Office
records.description: Government-funded but independent office that audits and oversees the health regulatory colleges and houses a new independent discipline tribunal for serious misconduct hearings.
records.note: The release says the Province established it in 2024, led by Superintendent Sherri Young, and that its work began April 1, 2026 when the Health Professions and Occupations Act took effect. The discipline tribunal inside it has no separate record because the release gives it no proper name.

records.name: Property Assessment Review Panels
records.description: First level of appeal for BC property assessments under the Assessment Act, hearing owners' complaints each year from February 1 to March 15.
records.note: Administratively accountable to the Ministry of Finance (tribunal-sector page); listed in the Finance 2026/27 service plan Appendix A.

records.name: Residential Tenancy Branch
records.description: Ministry branch that hears and resolves residential tenancy disputes between landlords and tenants.
records.note: A ministry branch rather than a statutory tribunal. The Housing 2026/27 service plan measures the share of RTB disputes heard within service standards.

records.name: Office of the BC Container Trucking Commissioner
records.description: Enforces the Container Trucking Act and issues Container Trucking Services licences for trucks serving Lower Mainland ports.
records.note: Established under the 2014 Container Trucking Act (OBCCTC site). Listed as 'BC Container Trucking Commission' in the Transportation 2026/27 service plan Appendix A.

records.name: Managed Forest Council
records.description: Independent provincial agency under the Private Managed Forest Land Act that regulates forest practices on private managed forest land.
records.note: 'Established in May 2004' (MFC home page); listed in the Forests 2026/27 service plan Appendix A.

gaps: Already top-level graph nodes, so no sub records written. Their administrative parents per the tribunal-sector page and 2026/27 service plans: labour-relations-board (AG per tribunal-sector page and AG plan; Labour plan also claims it), bc-human-rights-tribunal (AG), bc-utilities-commission (AG), agricultural-land-commission (Agriculture and Food), forest-practices-board (Forests).
Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch no longer exists: the Independent Gambling Control Office replaced it on April 13, 2026 (recorded).
Industry Training Appeal Board is now the Skilled Trades BC Appeal Board (recorded). No page read states the rename, so no former-name note was added.
Oil and Gas Appeal Tribunal is now the Energy Resource Appeal Tribunal (recorded).
Discipline tribunal under the Health Professions and Occupations Act (in force April 1, 2026): no official proper name found, so it is folded into the oversight-office record.

Not recorded, being delegated or self-governing regulators rather than tribunals: Consumer Protection BC, Vehicle Sales Authority of BC, Law Society of BC, Society of Notaries Public, Legal Professions BC (operational ~2027), Insurance Council of BC, Technical Safety BC (already a node), health regulatory colleges, and PSEFS professional-governance regulators.

Not recorded, being minor or advisory: the eight agricultural marketing boards and commissions under BCFIRB (listed in the AF service plan), the Notaries Public Board of Examiners (AG), the StudentAid BC Appeal Committee and Degree Quality Assessment Board (PSEFS), the Independent School Teaching Certificate Standards Committee (Education), and the Data Stewardship Committee and Drug Benefit Council (Health).

Establishment year left null where no page read states it: BCRB, BCAB, CCALAB, ERAT, FAC, HPRB, PTB, PAAB, SSAB, STBCAB, SRB, WCAT, EAAT, BC Ferry Commission, LCRB, PARP, RTB, the teacher-regulation bodies, and the Health boards.
BC Government Directory (dir.gov.bc.ca) is no longer public (IDIR login required), so it could not be used to confirm branch placement.
Emergency Medical Assistants Licensing Board and Medical Services Commission: the gov.bc.ca page URLs tried returned 404, so url is null.
